{
  "headline": "Electricians test useful tools while defending paid hours around repairs that still need people.",
  "whatTheyDo": [
    {
      "tag": "keep-going",
      "text": "**118 of 206** continue practical repairs, often keeping paper records or checking actual wages alongside existing work."
    },
    {
      "tag": "learn-ai",
      "text": "**106 of 206** choose new AI learning, such as paid trials comparing quotes or parts lists with completed repairs."
    },
    {
      "tag": "collective-action",
      "text": "**61 of 206** use collective action, seeking written hours, paid teaching or workload agreements through unions and workers' associations."
    },
    {
      "tag": "cut-spending",
      "text": "**45 of 206** reduce spending, cancelling optional subscriptions or postponing purchases while preserving essentials and partner agreements where specified."
    },
    {
      "tag": "save-more",
      "text": "**33 of 206** build savings, including thirty monthly from packed lunches only after extra food costs and essential bills."
    }
  ],
  "whatTheySay": [
    "**Office tasks change first**, they say, while wiring, fault-finding and electrical checks still need real people.",
    "**Prove the saving** with completed jobs, accurate parts and realistic travel and testing time before imposing faster schedules.",
    "**Share the gains** through paid learning and agreed hours, including office staff and juniors rather than shifting costs onto workers."
  ],
  "whatTheyThink": [
    "**Work and paid hours** can shrink while repairs remain, through tighter allowances, fewer fit-outs or stronger price competition.",
    "**Household risk** can start with a partner’s bookings, accounts or design work even while an electrician’s own repairs look secure.",
    "**Skills and judgement** need real time; a smaller group sees more fitting work or cheaper administration for a small business."
  ],
  "howTheyFeel": [
    "**Anxiety leads**: 106 are anxious and three alarmed about realistic own or household income risks.",
    "Another **eighty are uneasy** and seventeen calm; nobody is panicked.",
    "Average **worry is 2.46**, on a scale from one for calm to five for panicked."
  ],
  "differences": [
    {
      "group": "Money cushion",
      "text": "Average **worry** is 2.88 for thin cushions, 2.39 for moderate cushions and 2.06 for strong cushions."
    },
    {
      "group": "Life stage",
      "text": "Average **worry** rises from 2.12 among early-career electricians to 2.57 in midlife and 2.89 among those later in working life."
    },
    {
      "group": "Outlook",
      "text": "**Collective action** appears in 54 of 69 progressive interviews, compared with four of 69 centre and three of 68 traditional interviews."
    },
    {
      "group": "Adaptability",
      "text": "New **AI learning** appears in 62 of 69 steady interviews, 43 of 68 adaptive interviews and one of 69 resistant interviews."
    }
  ],
  "quotes": [
    {
      "id": "A29-13122",
      "name": "Daria Larsen",
      "text": "I could lose hours even while my tool bag stays busy."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-12123",
      "name": "Bianca Farah",
      "text": "I could be doing fine at work and still have the household take a hit when my partner's accounting job shrinks."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-12113",
      "name": "Emeka Mensah",
      "text": "More AI means more data centres and more electric cars, and everything needs wiring."

{
  "headline": "Fast AGI makes the interval before physical robots a household income problem, with almost everyone at least anxious.",
  "whatTheyDo": [
    {
      "tag": "seek-support",
      "text": "**105 seek support**, including available community advice, eligibility checks, family housing, childcare or help reading records."
    },
    {
      "tag": "keep-going",
      "text": "**85 keep going**, with examples including paid repair calls, supervised shifts and finishing an existing licence."
    },
    {
      "tag": "change-job",
      "text": "**82 seek different work**, including posted maintenance or service jobs with workable written pay and hours."
    },
    {
      "tag": "save-more",
      "text": "**68 save more**, for example adding extra monthly wage deposits or repaying a van loan or mortgage."
    },
    {
      "tag": "cut-spending",
      "text": "**63 cut spending**, cancelling subscriptions, meals out or unbooked trips while replacement income remains uncertain."
    }
  ],
  "whatTheySay": [
    "**The two dates** often frame public explanations: thinking tasks change first, with capable robots reaching hands-on work around 2031.",
    "**Paid routes** feature in public demands for training, notice and worker involvement before changes to hours.",
    "**Public reassurance** sometimes masks fear: several urge others to stay calm while privately expecting their own work to disappear."
  ],
  "whatTheyThink": [
    "**Household exposure** extends beyond electrical work: partners’ booking, accounts, claims and physical jobs also face cuts.",
    "**Reserves buy room**, but many distinguish months of expenses from a lifetime wage or a guaranteed employer.",
    "**Skills and retirement** need checking: licences cannot guarantee future work, while unverified later payments cannot fill the household budget."
  ],
  "howTheyFeel": [
    "**110 are alarmed** and one panicked; 94 are anxious and one uneasy, with none calm.",
    "**Average worry is 3.54** on the five-point scale; concrete plans coexist with expected wage gaps and sleepless calculations."
  ],
  "differences": [
    {

      "text": "Average worry rises from **3.19** with strong cushions (63 people) to **3.46** with moderate (71) and **3.92** with thin (72)."

      "group": "Life stage",
      "text": "Average worry is **3.44** among 81 younger workers, **3.53** among 81 midlife workers and **3.73** among 44 later-career workers."

    {
      "id": "A29-11111",
      "heading": "My partner or family also faces lost work.",
      "thinkIndex": 2,
      "thinkText": "Sam's **care work** and my wiring could both go in the same year.",
      "sourceSHA": "87cd218038d78e16cfa31c5c0bf183b5d24b4a2fa45b8e50527e739b78a0770f",
      "semanticJustification": "She fears the same-year loss of her wiring and her partner's care work, extending exposure across the household."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-11112",
      "heading": "Physical work faces a later robot shock.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "Kerr's **office work** dies in 2028, and stepladder work follows with robots in **2031**.",
      "sourceSHA": "756fe52b50b63e7f03d419d1cb199502b97893006d78b058d4dd1d464ff5083f",
      "semanticJustification": "He explicitly distinguishes office work disappearing in 2028 from stepladder work following in 2031."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-11113",
      "heading": "Physical work faces a later robot shock.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "Thinking AI makes me a better electrician just before robots arrive in **2031**.",
      "sourceSHA": "f663588f2e6cd6153841f5f7108a6eb3210e5812c91b9a6ba9f2149c80cc40c5",
      "semanticJustification": "She sees thinking AI improving her work before robots arrive in 2031, identifying a temporary physical-work interval."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-11121",
      "heading": "My current work or skills may not carry me through.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "By 2028 it's **too late** for me to learn AI.",
      "sourceSHA": "641aa27268f1e1964fe317c0dd4680a119b0de136623de29213599d34b2f04e8",
      "semanticJustification": "He believes the fast arrival leaves him too late to learn AI, questioning whether his present skills can get him through."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-11122",
      "heading": "My partner or family also faces lost work.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "Kai's depot goes **first** and my job goes **three years later**.",
      "sourceSHA": "052e44be38ed10434ece6771010a8c6273ec0ab12820b0e7d51ba0d72137913d",
      "semanticJustification": "She places Kai's depot loss ahead of her own job loss, explicitly considering the other earner's exposure."

    {
      "id": "A29-11123",
      "heading": "My current work or skills may not carry me through.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "New-build first fix is the **first hands-on job** robots would learn.",
      "sourceSHA": "3cf6404d8fa4f35bbf98abf2c8417cfc350d7e98fd39a0bab2cc04bb5d6f71fb",
      "semanticJustification": "He regards his repetitive first-fix work as the first physical task robots would learn, undermining his current route."

    {
      "id": "A29-11131",
      "heading": "My partner or family also faces lost work.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "Matt and I could lose our **trades** within the same few years.",
      "sourceSHA": "a56e329265f29b7eabf2a0d418a8daa80a6f7d27f35852e9325f882a1f14e971",
      "semanticJustification": "She fears both her and Matt's trades could disappear within the same few years."

    {

      "heading": "My partner or family also faces lost work.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "By 2031 robots fix the fryers and **my dad's shop** is squeezed.",
      "sourceSHA": "624b496ab0a1410b692a863cdf24daa7fac3d88da4e07d376de5761450d72bcc",
      "semanticJustification": "He expects his father's shop to be squeezed when robots repair fryers, extending the threat into family work."

    {
      "id": "A29-11133",
      "heading": "Physical work faces a later robot shock.",
      "thinkIndex": 1,
      "thinkText": "Robots in **2031** still scare me.",
      "sourceSHA": "c740b0cd44d2ae61f91c097a711b3bdc1b30296bfcab41a233f8f2fadb8ca27c",
      "semanticJustification": "She remains frightened by the 2031 robot arrival despite seeing a short business-starting window in the preceding private thought."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-11211",
      "heading": "My current work or skills may not carry me through.",
      "thinkIndex": 0,
      "thinkText": "I think the **junior's work** goes to robots before the boss's signature does.",
      "sourceSHA": "fbe5bf4c41c8f195b5942e33baafab6f96b3d2a3b0f0683170ec840b32c9736d",
      "semanticJustification": "He expects a robot to take junior work before the boss's signature, identifying the vulnerability of his present position."

    {
      "id": "A29-11212",
      "heading": "Physical work faces a later robot shock.",
      "thinkIndex": 1,
      "thinkText": "I don't know what happens once **robots** climb stairs in 2031.",

  "headline": "Five years opens practical routes, but most still worry about earnings and many households lack a confirmed replacement wage.",

      "text": "**107 of 206** choose training, from inspection qualifications to practical controls classes conditional on covered fees and protected wages."

"""Build scratch-only, accepted-manifest insight evidence and exact numerical census."""
import collections, hashlib, json, math, pathlib, subprocess, sys
ROOT=pathlib.Path('/workspace/Paradigm'); SCRATCH=pathlib.Path('/tmp/paradigm-s7-20261118/insights')
code=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else 'A29'
assert code in ['A29','A30','A31','A32']
status=json.loads((ROOT/'data/repass-status/session-7.json').read_text())
manifest={i:h for i,h in {**status['initialPassingHashes'],**status['acceptedNewHashes']}.items() if i.startswith(code+'-')}
assert len(manifest)>=200, 'Insights gate: at least 200 reviewed passing interviews required'
people=[]
for id,h in sorted(manifest.items()):
 p=ROOT/f'data/interviews/archetypes/raw/{id}.json'; assert hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==h,id
 d=json.loads(p.read_text()); assert d['protocolVersion']=='3.1'; people.append(d)
raw=[json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in (ROOT/'data/interviews/archetypes/raw').glob(code+'-*.json')]
assert {d['id'] for d in raw if d.get('protocolVersion')=='3.1'}==set(manifest), 'Finish review or pause raw drafts before insights; validator census must match reviewed manifest'
subprocess.run(['node','scripts/validate-archetype-interviews.mjs',code],cwd=ROOT,check=True,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
out=SCRATCH/f'{code}-{len(people)}';out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(out/'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2)+'\n')
grid=json.loads((ROOT/'data/archetypes/grid.json').read_text()); moods=['calm','uneasy','anxious','alarmed','panicked']; scenarios={}; evidence=[]
round2=lambda x: math.floor(x*100+0.5)/100
for sc in ['S0','S1','S2','S3','S4']:
 def census(sub):
  n=len(sub); c=collections.Counter(a for p in sub for a in set(p['scenarios'][sc]['actions']))
  return {'n':n,'avgWorry':round2(sum(moods.index(p['scenarios'][sc]['mood'])+1 for p in sub)/n) if n else 0,'moodMix':{m:sum(p['scenarios'][sc]['mood']==m for p in sub) for m in moods},'actions':[{'tag':a,'count':v,'share':round2(v/n)} for a,v in sorted(c.items(),key=lambda z:(-z[1],z[0]))]}
 x=census(people);x['byGroup']={g['key']:[{'level':l['key'],**census([p for p in people if p['levels'][g['key']]==l['key']])} for l in g['levels']] for g in grid['groups']}
 x['segmentIds']={}
 for end,order in [('least',moods),('most',list(reversed(moods)))]:
  ids=[]
  for m in order:
   ids.extend(p['id'] for p in people if p['scenarios'][sc]['mood']==m)
   if len(ids)>=5:break
  x['segmentIds'][end]=sorted(ids)
 scenarios[sc]=x
 for p in people:
  q=p['scenarios'][sc]
  evidence.append({'id':p['id'],'name':p['name'],'scenario':sc,'sha256':manifest[p['id']],'levels':p['levels'],'think':[{'index':i,'text':t} for i,t in enumerate(q['think'])],'say':q['say'],'do':q['do'],'feel':q['feel'],'mood':q['mood'],'quote':q['quote'],'actions':q['actions'],'steps':q['steps']})
(out/'stats.json').write_text(json.dumps({'code':code,'interviews':len(people),'scenarios':scenarios},indent=2)+'\n')
(out/'sources.jsonl').write_text(''.join(json.dumps(e,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n' for e in evidence))
print(out)

{
  "headline": "Electricians test useful tools while defending paid hours around repairs that still need people.",
  "whatTheyDo": [
    {
      "tag": "keep-going",
      "text": "**119 of 206** continue practical repairs, often keeping paper records or checking actual wages alongside existing work."
    },
    {
      "tag": "learn-ai",
      "text": "**105 of 206** choose new AI learning, such as paid trials comparing quotes or parts lists with completed repairs."
    },
    {
      "tag": "collective-action",
      "text": "**61 of 206** act collectively, seeking written hours, paid teaching or workload agreements through unions, associations or agreed joint requests."
    },
    {
      "tag": "cut-spending",
      "text": "**45 of 206** reduce spending, cancelling optional subscriptions or postponing purchases while preserving essentials and partner agreements where specified."
    },
    {
      "tag": "save-more",
      "text": "**33 of 206** build savings, including thirty monthly from packed lunches only after extra food costs and essential bills."
    }
  ],
  "whatTheySay": [
    "**Office tasks change first**, they say, while wiring, fault-finding and electrical checks still need real people.",
    "**Prove the saving** with completed jobs, accurate parts and realistic travel and testing time before imposing faster schedules.",
    "**Share the gains** through paid learning and agreed hours, including office staff and juniors rather than shifting costs onto workers."
  ],
  "whatTheyThink": [
    "**Work and paid hours** can shrink while repairs remain, through tighter allowances, fewer fit-outs or stronger price competition.",
    "**Household risk** can start with a partner’s bookings, accounts or design work even while an electrician’s own repairs look secure.",
    "**Skills and judgement** need real time; a smaller group sees more fitting work or cheaper administration for a small business."
  ],
  "howTheyFeel": [
    "**Anxiety leads**: 106 are anxious and three alarmed about realistic own or household income risks.",
    "Another **eighty are uneasy** and seventeen calm; nobody is panicked.",
    "Average **worry is 2.46**, on a scale from one for calm to five for panicked."
  ],
  "differences": [
    {
      "group": "Money cushion",
      "text": "Average **worry** is 2.88 for thin cushions, 2.39 for moderate cushions and 2.06 for strong cushions."
    },
    {
      "group": "Life stage",
      "text": "Average **worry** rises from 2.12 among early-career electricians to 2.57 in midlife and 2.89 among those later in working life."
    },
    {
      "group": "Outlook",
      "text": "**Collective action** appears in 54 of 69 progressive interviews, compared with four of 69 centre and three of 68 traditional interviews."
    },
    {
      "group": "Adaptability",
      "text": "New **AI learning** appears in 61 of 69 steady interviews, 43 of 68 adaptive interviews and one of 69 resistant interviews."
    }
  ],
  "quotes": [
    {
      "id": "A29-13122",
      "name": "Daria Larsen",
      "text": "I could lose hours even while my tool bag stays busy."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-12123",
      "name": "Bianca Farah",
      "text": "I could be doing fine at work and still have the household take a hit when my partner's accounting job shrinks."
    },
    {
      "id": "A29-12113",
      "name": "Emeka Mensah",
      "text": "More AI means more data centres and more electric cars, and everything needs wiring."
    }

    "**The two dates** often frame public explanations: thinking tasks change first, with capable robots reaching hands-on work around 2031.",

    "**Public reassurance** sometimes masks fear: several urge others to stay calm while privately expecting their own work to disappear."

{
  "headline": "Five years opens practical routes, but most still worry about earnings and many households lack a confirmed replacement wage.",
  "whatTheyDo": [
    {
      "tag": "retrain",
      "text": "**107 of 206** choose training, from inspection qualifications to practical controls classes conditional on covered fees and protected wages."
    },
    {
      "tag": "keep-going",
      "text": "**87 of 206** continue current work, including licensed repairs and supervised junior tasks, while checking hours or household resources."
    },
    {
      "tag": "save-more",
      "text": "**83 of 206** save or repay debt, from meal-budget transfers to mortgage overpayments; several require essentials covered and existing reserves protected."
    },
    {
      "tag": "change-job",
      "text": "**63 of 206** seek different paid work; several retain current jobs until signed pay, hours and travel terms fit."
    },
    {
      "tag": "seek-support",
      "text": "**53 of 206** seek advice, record help or household support, checking actual resources rather than assuming replacement income."
    }
  ],
  "whatTheySay": [
    "**Start now** is the common public message: seek usable paid learning, clearer work terms and plans before the thinking-work change.",
    "**Physical robots follow later**; several include office workers and partners rather than treating site workers’ preparation window as everyone’s.",
    "**Preparation needs paid work**, with repeated requests for fees, protected weekly wages and actual tasks instead of course links."
  ],
  "whatTheyThink": [
    "**More time helps** some qualify, test paid routes, build businesses or strengthen reserves; others still question lasting paid demand.",
    "**Household gaps remain** when partner desk income is exposed, current bills are tight or later physical work faces robot competition.",
    "**Older workers need figures**, including verified retirement income and actual suitable work; birthdays and savings balances do not confirm affordable stopping."
  ],
  "howTheyFeel": [
    "**Anxious remains largest**: 112 of 206; 64 are uneasy, 29 alarmed and one calm; none are panicked.",
    "**Extra warning isn’t income**: alarmed interviewees still describe expected large household losses and sleeplessness while making practical plans.",

      "group": "Adaptability",
      "text": "**Steady adapters** retrain 47/69 (68%), versus 26/69 (38%) resistant and 34/68 (50%) adaptive workers; these are chosen actions, not guaranteed outcomes."
